scope.subject: A healthy, mature, mammalian skeletal muscle fiber shown as a shortened cylindrical segment with a longitudinal cutaway.
scope.cutawayDisclosure: The removed shell and exposed interior are an artificial learning view, not a natural opening in the cell.
scope.scaleDisclosure: Membranes, organelles, sarcomere bands, spaces, and vessels are enlarged or separated selectively for legibility and are not mutually to scale.

observedSourcesPreferred: adult mammalian skeletal muscle light microscopy
electron microscopy of longitudinal and transverse sections
three-dimensional microscopy where spatial placement is asserted
referencePolicy.singleViewLimit: A single illustration or render cannot validate the rear surface, cutaway depth, internal connectivity, or organelle distribution.

orientation.longAxis: All myofibrils and repeated sarcomeres run parallel to the fiber long axis.
orientation.transverseAxis: Z discs and sarcomere bands form transverse registrations across neighboring myofibrils at learning scale.
orientation.outsideInsideRule: The capillary remains extracellular; myonuclei, myofibrils, SR, T-tubules, and mitochondria are intracellular.

semanticStructures.label: Skeletal muscle fiber
semanticStructures.geometryContract: One elongated volumetric cell segment with a long axis, transverse cut face, intact rear/underside volume, and an intentional longitudinal cutaway exposing internal systems.
semanticStructures.placementContract: Root semantic object containing the sarcolemma, sarcoplasm, myonuclei, myofibrils, SR/T-tubules, and mitochondria; the capillary remains outside this root cell volume.
reviewFailures: bundle of multiple muscle fibers labelled as one fiber
single-view relief or hollow shell
loss of cell volume at rear, sides, ends, top, or bottom

semanticStructures.label: Sarcolemma
semanticStructures.geometryContract: A continuous volumetric cylindrical cell boundary with modelled thickness at cut edges. The T-tubule is continuous with this membrane as an inward invagination.
semanticStructures.placementContract: Outermost cellular boundary; must enclose sarcoplasm and all intracellular structures.
reviewFailures: open accidental holes outside the intentional cutaway
paper-thin cut edge with no readable thickness
capillary placed inside the membrane
T-tubule floating independently of the membrane

semanticStructures.label: Myonucleus
semanticStructures.geometryContract: Several elongated or flattened nuclei distributed along the segment; do not use one central spherical nucleus as the normal mature state.
semanticStructures.placementContract: Peripheral and intracellular, immediately beneath the sarcolemma, with spacing along the fiber rather than a dense cluster.
reviewFailures: only one nucleus
nuclei outside the sarcolemma
normal adult fiber depicted with predominantly central nuclei
confusing an external satellite-cell nucleus with a myonucleus
semanticStructures.caveat: Central myonuclei can occur during development, regeneration, loading responses, or disease; this asset represents a healthy mature mammalian fiber.

semanticStructures.label: Sarcoplasm
semanticStructures.geometryContract: A continuous intracellular matrix occupying readable but modest spaces around and between myofibrils and organelles.
semanticStructures.placementContract: Inside the sarcolemma and outside the interiors of organelles and myofibrils.
reviewFailures: rendered as an empty hollow cavity
rendered as an external coating
so much open space that myofibrils no longer read as densely packed

semanticStructures.label: Myofibril
semanticStructures.geometryContract: Many densely packed, parallel, longitudinal contractile cylinders. At least one must be exposed or enlarged enough to resolve repeating sarcomeres.
semanticStructures.placementContract: Runs along the fiber long axis; neighboring myofibrils should register their striations approximately transversely.
reviewFailures: randomly oriented bundles
a single central rod standing in for the fiber interior
striations painted only on the sarcolemma
featureless rear or underside interior

semanticStructures.label: Sarcomere
semanticStructures.geometryContract: A repeating longitudinal unit bounded by two Z discs. The learning-scale band order must be Z disc, half I band, A band, half I band, next Z disc.
semanticStructures.placementContract: Repeated in series along each myofibril, with shared Z-disc boundaries between adjacent units.
reviewFailures: sarcomere boundaries not tied to Z discs
irregular decorative striping with no consistent band order
neighboring sarcomeres represented as disconnected beads

semanticStructures.label: Z disc
semanticStructures.geometryContract: A narrow transverse disc or line marking each sarcomere boundary and bisecting the I-band region shared by adjacent sarcomeres.
semanticStructures.placementContract: Perpendicular to the myofibril long axis; successive discs define sarcomere length.
reviewFailures: placed at the center of the A band
drawn as a longitudinal stripe
omitted from the contraction state

semanticStructures.label: A band
semanticStructures.geometryContract: A broad central band corresponding to the full length of the thick filaments; shown consistently across repeated sarcomeres.
semanticStructures.placementContract: Centered between Z discs and flanked by I-band regions.
reviewFailures: A band shown at a Z disc
A-band width changing during the contraction demonstration
alternating band sequence that implies discontinuous thick filaments

semanticStructures.label: I band
semanticStructures.geometryContract: A lighter or otherwise distinguishable thin-filament-only region bordering each A band; each Z disc lies within the continuous I-band region shared across a sarcomere boundary.
semanticStructures.placementContract: Between the edge of an A band and the Z disc on each side.
reviewFailures: I band placed at the sarcomere center
I band omitted entirely
I-band width held fixed in a claimed shortening animation

semanticStructures.label: Sarcoplasmic reticulum
semanticStructures.geometryContract: A connected network of longitudinal tubules and enlarged terminal cisternae wrapping around myofibrils, presented selectively rather than as an opaque sleeve.
semanticStructures.placementContract: Interfibrillar and intracellular; closely associated with each displayed myofibril and continuous with terminal cisternae.
reviewFailures: isolated decorative loops with no network continuity
placed outside the sarcolemma
fused visually with the T-tubule as one membrane compartment

semanticStructures.label: T-tubule
semanticStructures.geometryContract: A transverse inward continuation of the sarcolemma that penetrates the fiber and remains a distinct membrane system from the SR.
semanticStructures.placementContract: At the A-I junction in the adult mammalian reference model; one T-tubule passes between two terminal cisternae to form a triad.
reviewFailures: closed intracellular tube with no continuity to sarcolemma
longitudinal orientation presented as typical
merged into the SR lumen
semanticStructures.caveat: Triad position varies among vertebrate groups and developmental states; A-I-junction placement is the adult mammalian convention used here.

semanticStructures.label: Terminal cisterna
semanticStructures.geometryContract: Two enlarged SR sacs flanking a central T-tubule without becoming continuous with its lumen.
semanticStructures.placementContract: One on each side of the T-tubule at a displayed A-I junction.
reviewFailures: only one cisterna in a structure labelled triad
cisternae located inside the T-tubule
no connection to longitudinal SR

semanticStructures.label: Triad
semanticStructures.geometryContract: Exactly one central T-tubule closely apposed to two terminal cisternae, one on either side; members remain pickable as their own semantic parts.
semanticStructures.placementContract: At an A-I junction in the adult mammalian reference model; a teaching close-up may enlarge one representative triad.
reviewFailures: dyad labelled as triad
three identical tubes
triad placed randomly with no sarcomere landmark
junction floating away from a myofibril

semanticStructures.label: Mitochondrion
semanticStructures.geometryContract: Several elongated or ovoid organelles, not a uniform shell or dense carpet. A simplified inner fold cue may be enlarged for recognition.
semanticStructures.placementContract: Representative interfibrillar mitochondria lie between myofibrils; representative peripheral mitochondria may lie beneath the sarcolemma and near nuclei or a capillary groove.
reviewFailures: inside myofibril contractile material
inside capillary lumen
uniform abundance implied for all fiber types
all mitochondria restricted to one arbitrary cluster
semanticStructures.caveat: Mitochondrial abundance, shape, connectivity, and subcellular distribution vary strongly with fiber type, metabolic state, muscle, species, and sampling method.

semanticStructures.label: Capillary
semanticStructures.geometryContract: A narrow vessel segment following the outside of the fiber; it may occupy a shallow surface groove but retains its own wall and lumen.
semanticStructures.placementContract: Extracellular, alongside the sarcolemma and approximately parallel or gently oblique to the fiber long axis. It may indent the surface but must never enter the sarcoplasm.
reviewFailures: capillary lumen inside the muscle cell
capillary presented as a T-tubule
vessel crossing freely through myofibrils
claiming one vessel serves only one fiber
semanticStructures.caveat: A capillary is shared within the endomysial microvascular network; the close apposition shown is representative, not a complete vascular map.

mustShow: thin and thick filaments increase their overlap without the filaments themselves shortening
mayShowIfIncluded: modest transverse fiber expansion when whole-fiber shortening is animated
calcium-release direction as a symbolic overlay clearly labelled schematic
mustNotClaimOrShow: sarcomeres along one myofibril contracting out of sequence as the normal mechanism
nuclei or mitochondria actively producing contractile force
the cutaway peeling open during physiological contraction
exact force, velocity, calcium concentration, or time course unless driven by a separately validated quantitative model
contractionDemonstration.disclosure: Animation is a qualitative sliding-filament teaching model. Distances and timing are exaggerated for visibility and do not constitute a biomechanical simulation.

minimumScientificAcceptance: The fiber reads as one long multinucleated cell, not a bundle of separate cells.
The uncut remainder, rear, sides, and ends retain real volume under unrestricted orbit.
Several peripheral myonuclei lie beneath an enclosing sarcolemma.
Many longitudinal myofibrils occupy the sarcoplasm and display consistent transverse striation registration.
At least one learning-scale sarcomere clearly resolves Z discs, A band, and I bands in correct order.
At least one triad resolves one T-tubule plus two distinct SR terminal cisternae at an A-I junction.
The T-tubule is continuous with the sarcolemma; terminal cisternae are continuous with the SR, not with the T-tubule lumen.
Representative mitochondria occupy plausible interfibrillar and/or subsarcolemmal spaces without implying uniform fiber-type abundance.
The capillary is extracellular and may lie in a sarcolemmal surface groove without entering the fiber.
Any contraction state preserves A-band width while narrowing I bands and shortening Z-to-Z distance.
All scale exaggerations, omitted structures, and synthetic-hypothesis views are disclosed.
knownSimplifications: Molecular proteins, myofilament lattice geometry, M line, H zone, costameres, basal lamina, endomysium, motor end plate, satellite cells, and complete microvascular branching may be omitted unless separately implemented and reviewed.
A small representative subset of myofibrils, sarcomeres, SR membranes, mitochondria, nuclei, and capillaries stands in for much larger biological counts.
Colors are semantic teaching colors rather than native tissue colors.
The cutaway may spatially separate tightly packed structures so learners can select them.
Adult mammalian organization is not universal across species, development, regeneration, or disease.
